distractors.alternate_meaning: Trunk also means the central region of the human body.
A chest is also a storage container.
To box is to fight with one's fists.
A grand piano is an instrument, rather than grand meaning excellent.
Upright also describes honorable conduct.
A noble is a member of the aristocracy.
A nerve cell is a neuron.
A stem is the supporting part of a flower.
Pistil sounds like pistol.
A box office sells admission tickets.
A headache is a pain; closed compounds are allowed.
A necktie is worn around the neck; closed compounds are allowed.
Rye is a cereal grain as well as a bread name.
Cornflakes are a breakfast cereal.
A potato chip is a thin fried snack.
Pinpoint is an exact position; the blank may form a closed compound.
A breakwater protects a harbor; closed compounds are allowed.
Tap is a dance style, rather than a water faucet.
Olive oil is a cooking oil.
A palm is a tree as well as part of the hand.
To pine is to long for something.
Punch also means a mixed drink served at parties.
A soda fountain dispenses carbonated drinks.
A garden party is an outdoor social event.
A case study examines a particular instance.
A timetable lists scheduled times.
A card shark is a skilled or dishonest card player.
A flat tire has lost its air.
A front page is the first page of a newspaper.
Backstage is the area behind a theater stage; closed compounds are allowed.
To roast someone is to mock them.
A jeer is a vocal expression of mockery.
Scream is the exact title of a horror film.
Boston terrier names a dog breed.
A border can mean an outer limit.
Fringe is a decorative trimming of dangling threads.
A jingle is a short musical advertisement.
A flyer can be an animal capable of flight.
The butterfly effect describes sensitivity to initial conditions.
Junk food is food with little nutritional value.
A soulmate is a close companion; closed compounds are allowed.
To ship is to send goods.
A short circuit is an unintended electrical path.
Open can mean accessible or available for use.
Passable can mean adequate rather than navigable.
